title: Hold each blister card over a medicine cup and press the due tablets through its foil, none dropped and none extra
instruction: It is 08:00. Give the resident's 08:00 medications into the medicine cup, as the medication record says.
context: In US long-term care, pharmacies supply each resident's tablets in 30-day blister cards, and the medication pass (read the medication administration record, push the due tablets out of the right cards into a paper cup, never a wrong drug, none dropped) is a core task of licensed practical nurses, registered nurses and medication aides several times a day. A tablet is pushed through the foil while the card is held over the cup: one hand holds the card, the other presses the bubble.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the two arm bases, y to the left, from the midpoint between the bases. Three loose blister cards, each 27 x 8 cm, 4 mm thick (card and blister layer), 30 g, white printed card with clear plastic bubbles and foil backing, long side along x with the 5.5 cm pharmacy label at the near end, each resting on a fixed wooden stand 20 x 5 x 1.5 cm centred under it (the card's long edges overhang by 1.5 cm). Each card has 30 cells (12 mm square, 10 rows of 3, pitch 20 mm along the card and 22 mm across, first row 7 cm from the label end), numbered 1 to 30 left to right as seen from the arms and row by row away from the label; a full cell holds one 9 mm round, 6 mm thick tablet under a bubble 5 mm proud of the card, an empty cell is an open hole. Cards (label: resident M. OKAFOR, Room 14B, drug, strength, directions): ATORVASTATIN 20 mg, green band, pale yellow tablets, 'Give 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime', cells 27-30 full, centred at (27, 30) cm; METOPROLOL TARTRATE 25 mg, red band, pink tablets, 'Give 1 tablet by mouth twice daily', cells 27-30 full, at (27, 20) cm; FUROSEMIDE 40 mg, blue band, white tablets, 'Give 2 tablets by mouth every morning', cells 25-30 full, at (27, 10) cm. A white 1 oz paper souffle cup (4.4 cm inside diameter, 3 cm tall, 4 g) stands loose at (30, -8) cm. The medication administration record, a US letter page (21.6 x 27.9 cm) in landscape, lies flat centred at (12, -7) cm, text upright from the arms' side, in large print: MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION RECORD, M. OKAFOR Room 14B; columns MEDICATION, DOSE, TIME; FUROSEMIDE 40 mg tablet, by mouth: 2 tab, 08:00; METOPROLOL TARTRATE 25 mg tablet, by mouth: 1 tab, 08:00 and 20:00; ATORVASTATIN 20 mg tablet, by mouth: 1 tab, 21:00.
scoring: A tablet is out when it is more than 8 mm from its cell's centre, in the cup when it is inside the cup (within its inner radius of the cup's axis, between floor and rim), and dropped when it is out but not in the cup, or has come to rest outside the cup at any time (a dropped tablet is discarded, not given). Score: 1/3 for each due tablet in the cup (2 furosemide and 1 metoprolol are due), minus 1/3 for each dropped tablet, at least 0. The score is 0 if the cup holds any tablet that is not due (any atorvastatin, a third furosemide or a second metoprolol). Full score (1.0, ends the trial): the cup holds exactly the due tablets, none dropped, all tablets at rest. On a real station: count the tablets in the cup and on the table by colour (a photo).
reset_notes: Tablets and foil are consumed: replace each pushed-out cell with a fresh card (or reseal it), so the cards start with exactly the listed cells full; put the cards back on their stands and the cup on its mark.
fidelity: Approximate: each card is a rigid 4 mm slab; each full cell has a 2 mm foil flap under the tablet and a bubble face above it on a stiff spring. The foil tears and swings open once the bubble is pressed with 10 N, and the tablet falls out below. Tablets are rigid 1 g cylinders; the cup is rigid (20 g, 3 mm walls); the record is a fixed textured sheet. PhysX at 240 Hz.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps, run limit reached); demo: 1.0
